subject: Temporary rate-tier carveout request for ML retraining window
messages:
From: Aisha Menon <aisha.menon@olympus.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 08 Jan 2027 17:02:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary rate-tier carveout for Jan 15-18 retrain

Hi Rachel,

Quick note from the ML ops side at Olympus — we have a hard retraining window the weekend of Jan 15-18 to roll a new recommendation model. The retrain pipeline will spike inference traffic (online feature validation + scoring) briefly but at high QPS for roughly 36 hours.

We understand Redwood's fairness and burst policies, but this workload is time-sensitive (regulatory data snapshot alignment). Can we request a temporary rate-tier carveout that:
- increases our burst allowance to 3x for a 36-hour window (UTC 2027-01-16 04:00 to 2027-01-17 16:00)
- suspends per-customer throttling exceptions for that window (we will still accept longer tail latencies)

Attached is a traffic projection CSV and a short note on the service dependencies. We want to ensure uptime/latency SLAs do not get materially impacted for other tenants — happy to accept guardrails (canary runs, traffic shaping) you require.

Procurement copied on this thread — please confirm if this requires a formal amendment.

Thanks,
Aisha Menon
Head of ML Infrastructure, Olympus AI
aisha.menon@olympus.ai

Attachments: mlops_traffic_projection_q1.csv

Date: Fri, 08 Jan 2027 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate-tier carveout for Jan 15-18 retrain

Thanks Aisha — appreciate the context and the projection file. Looping in Karthik (infra) and Neha (Customer Ops) to assess operational impact and guardrails. A few initial asks from our side:

- Can you run a 2-hour canary against a representative prefix prior to the window (we can schedule a small golden traffic test at +24h).
- Confirm whether you can fall back to a quantized scoring variant for 20% of traffic if latency exceeds 2s.
- We will need a procurement note if you want us to temporarily relax fairness policies — legal may require an amendment for commercial carveouts.

Karthik/Neha — any red flags from infra or fairness side? If we can approve a limited carveout, we will specify firm start/end times, throttling ceilings, and a one-time uplift fee.

I can coordinate a short WAR room (30m) early next week if helpful.

—Rachel

Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate-tier carveout for Jan 15-18 retrain

Hi team,

Reviewed the projection — main constraints and proposed controls below:

Constraints:
- Our fairness scheduler enforces a per-customer token/QPS budget; without explicit carveout, we will throttle once steady-state QPS is reached.
- A full suspension of fairness across the host would risk tail latency for small tenants; we cannot grant a global suspend.

Proposed operational carveout (conditional):
1) Window: 2027-01-16 04:00 UTC -> 2027-01-17 16:00 UTC (36 hours)
2) Burst: allow up to 3x of baseline QPS for the tenant, but gated by an overall host ceiling to protect others.
3) Canary: Olympus runs a 2-hour canary on 2027-01-15 16:00 UTC; we run parallel sampling and monitor 95/99 p95/p99 latency.
4) Fallback: if p95 > 2s for > 10 minutes, automatically shift 25% of traffic to a quantized variant (we can coordinate a split).
5) Logging: enable elevated trace sampling for the window; Redwood will export an audit bundle within 24 hours post-window.

Commercial / SLA implications:
- This is a temporary operational exception; our baseline uptime SLA (99.9%) remains. However, latency SLOs may see transient degradation under heavy host-wide conditions — we will provide credits if host-level p99 breaches > 15 minutes (terms in attached docx).
- Legal requires a one-off amendment to record the carveout and the uplift.

Attached: proposed_carveout_terms.docx (draft) and I'll upload canary templates after we confirm schedule.

If that framework works for Olympus, we can move to commercial terms and a docusign.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: proposed_carveout_terms.docx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 11:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate-tier carveout for Jan 15-18 retrain

Quick commercial note — happy to support a one-time carveout with the following commercial guardrails:
- One-time uplift fee equivalent to 20% of the expected monthly usage for Jan (billed pro-rata).
- If host-level p99 latency degradation (across tenants) exceeds agreed threshold for >15 minutes, Olympus receives a credit equal to 50% of the uplift for each additional 30-minute block, capped at 100% of the uplift.
- Procurement amendment to be executed via DocuSign.

If legal approves the attached doc, I can sign off and Rachel can send the DocuSign link.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
